text: A tucked tail and lowered body posture can be associated with fear, discomfort, or uncertainty. These signs should be considered together with the surrounding situation.
A dog holding its ears backward may be displaying uncertainty or discomfort. Ear position should be interpreted with other body language signals.
Dogs may demonstrate playful behavior through loose movements, play bows, and changes in body posture. Observing the entire interaction is important.
Stiff posture and sudden stillness may indicate heightened attention or tension. These signals alone do not establish aggressive intent.
When a dog appears uncomfortable, increasing distance from a possible stressor and avoiding forced interactions may help. Professional guidance may be appropriate for ongoing behavioral concerns.
